AF Hassan Ariff, with MA Sobhan, Advocates—For Opposite Party Nos. 1-5
parties:
Abu Aslam (Md) Advocate, Member, Rajshahi District Bar Association ------ Petitioner
vs

full_judgment:
2. Facts giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration that the appointments of 546 employees (3rd & 4th class) are illegal, collusive, malafide and against the interest of Rajshahi University and for permanent injunction restraining the defendant Nos. 1-5 from confirming the said appointments and also prayed for temporary injunction restraining them from giving salaries and assigning any duties to the said employees. 

 3. The plaintiff-petitioner stated in his plaint, inter alia, that the plaintiff is a Lawyer and a member of Rajshahi District Bar Association. Rajshahi University is a national institution and being a citizen of the country he is obliged to protect its interest as well as the interest of the nation and hence filed the suit in public interest as a conscious citizen. The plaintiff alleged that the Rajshahi University (defendant No. 1) is an autonomous body and its administration, appointments, promotions and control of all teachers and employees and admission of its students are regulated under the Rajshahi University Act as well as the notifications and circulars of the University Grants Commission, hereinafter referred as UGC, that the UGC by a circular dated 28-5-03 declared that their should be no appointment in excess of the budget of the University and in appointing its teachers, officers and employees the guidelines of the UGC must be followed, that no appointment under Master Roll on the basis of daily payment should be given from 1-6-2003 and in case of appointment of employees its 50% posts should be filled from the sons/daughters heirs of the retired employees. But the Rajshahi University Authority illegally appointed 546 persons as 3rd and 4th Class employees on 15-4-2004 in an unprecedented manner and without following the established rules to fulfil personal and political interest of defendant Nos. 2-5 and against the interest of Rajshahi University (defendant No. 1). It is further stated that there was no necessity of such huge employees and no demand from the concerned departments for such appointments even in some cases there was no post and there was no public notice and advertisement for such appointments. It has been further stated that the Teachers Association of Rajshahi University observed strike in protest of the aforesaid illegal appointments and educational environment of the University has been disturbed and the University would suffer a loss of Taka 1,25,00,000 every year for such illegal appointments causing unnecessary huge financial burden and expenditure of the University striking at its financial strength to exist, etc. Hence, the plaintiff has thus filed the suit for public interest and to protect the said national institution. The plaintiff-petitioner also filed an application under Order XXXIX, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the similar fact along with relevant documents filed by way of First for an order of temporary injunction against defendant Nos. 1-5 restraining them from confirming of their appointments and from giving salaries and assigning duties to them till disposal of the suit. 

 4. The defendant-opposite parties 1-5 and 7, 10, 23, 28, 32, 35, 41, 42, 44, 52, 53, 54, 56, 60 and 64 appeared and filed two sets of written objections. Defendant-opposite party Nos. 1-5 contested the application denying the material averments of the application and stating in their written objections, in short, inter alia, that the plaintiff has no prima facie case, the balance of convenience and inconvenience is against him, that the restriction on appointment was withdrawn by the UGC on 22-12-2003 and restriction imposed by the Government was also withdrawn on 8-1-2004 by two separate circulars that in a meeting held on 22-3-2004 a decision for appointment of 327 4th Class employees on the daily basis was approved following due process and a decision for 219 3rd Class employees against vacant and non-created posts was approved on 24-3-04 by a duly constituted committee. Their further case is that said 546 (3rd and 4th class) employees were permitted to work in the interest of the University and already joined in their respective places of works and those employees along with their family members would be thrown in the street if they are removed or disturbed in their employment in any manner. They further stated that the internal administration and management of the University, its Departments. Halls and Faculties would be seriously affected, disturbed and interfered if the injunction is granted. They contends that the appointments have been made in good faith, in due process of law and for the interest of the University for which the plaintiff would not suffer any loss, etc the other set of written objections contends, inter alia, in short, that these answering defendants were not involved in appointing the said 546 employees in any manner and it was done violating the rules of the University and even there was no demand for such appointments from the respective offices departments and Falls and that the Chairman Council in its meeting dated 19-4-04 expressed their concern against such illegal appointments and demanded withdrawal of the newly appointed employees. Their further case is that since the appointments have been made excluding the employees who were already, in work, it created embarrassment of the Chairmen of different departments, etc. 

 5. The learned Senior Assistant Judge. Sadar by his order dated 23-6-04 allowed the said application on contest and granted temporary injunction restraining the defendant Nos. 1-5 from assigning any duties and giving salaries to said 546 employees and confirming their appointments on daily basis. That the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1-5 being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of temporary injunction filed Miscellaneous, Appeal No. 50 of 2004 before the learned District Judge, Rajshahi. The Miscellaneous Appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge 2nd Court, Rajshahi and the same was allowed by the impugned judgment and order dated 14-7-04 setting aside and vacating the order of temporary injunction passed by the trial Court. Hence this Rule at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner. 

 7. Trial Court allowing the application for temporary injunction observed and found that all appointments of the University were barred till 22-12-2003 and the bar was withdrawn by a circular of the UGC dated 22-12-2003 and the restrictions imposed by the Government was also withdrawn on 8-1-04 by two separate circulars allowing to make necessary appointment as per prevailing rule and procedure. But the proposal of appointment of 546 employees was not communicated to the Government through UGC for approval nor the Government or the UGC approved the same. A new set of work-charged appointments were made on daily basis in Master Roll defying and without fulfilling the terms of the circular dated 4-11-1997 issued by the Registrar of the University malafide and illegally in order to remove the existing sets of employees of the same nature, that the appointments were made whimsically which is clear from the office order dated 31-5-04 of the defendant No. 2, the Vice-Chancellor of Rajshahi University, that the Rajshahi University Teachers Association in its meeting held on 20-4-04 demanded withdrawal of appointments of the said employees. The trial Court also found that there was neither any requirement nor demand nor proposal from the departmental heads nor there was any proposal from the Planning Committee of the University for such unprecedented huge number of appointments at a time, that there was no advertisement or notification in any dailies for such appointments and the appointments were made by the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 secretly by misusing their power to make the University a 'Lilla Boarding' and against the principle of natural justice on nepotism and favouritism instead of following the rules and procedures. The Trial Court having found a good prima facie arguable case, balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner loss and injury to the University granted temporary injunction. 

 8. The learned Additional District Judge set aside and vacated the order of injunction on the finding that the claim of irreparable loss and injury to the University due to aforesaid appointments does not appear as correct, that the plaintiff has no prima facie arguable case and he will not suffer any irreparable loss and injury personally for such appointments, that the order of injunction denying the salaries of the said employees at this stage does not arise, that the University will suffer inconvenience in morning its routine works, that the balance of convenience and inconvenience is against the plaintiff and that the trial Court gave finding on the merit of the suit in passing the order of temporary injunction improperly, etc. 

 9. Mr MI Farooqui, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner in support of the Rule, submits that the plaintiff-petitioner is an Advocate and a Member of Rajshahi Bar Association and being a patriotic and conscious citizen of the country brought the suit and the application for injunction to protest the illegal appointments and to resist drainage of public money in national interest in general and in the interest of Rajshahi University in particular. He submits that the appointments of 546 3rd and 4th Class employees were made by the vested group of the University in an unprecedented manner secretly and malafide without any public notification and in violation of the circulars, decisions, guidelines, rules and procedures etc, of the Government, UGC's and the University itself and without requirement of the departmental and faculties heads, decisions of the Rajshahi University Teachers Association. budgetary provisions, etc, provided for such appointments and violating the principle of natural justice and in malafide with bad motive to remove the existing Master Roll employees of the same nature by the new set of employees. He submits that the trial Court in consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the rules and guidelines provided therefore passed the order of injunction on finding a good prima facie arguable case and balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner to prevent the irreparable loss of the University likely to be caused by those appointments made contrary to the rules, procedure and guidelines laid down for such appointment and in breach of the circulars and budgetary provision of Rajshahi University. He also canvassed that the other set of defendants who filed their written objections also admitted the irregularity and illegality, breach and violation of rules and procedures, circulars and the guidelines in making these appointments by the contesting defendant and there was no demand from the departmental heads and they themselves failed to show that the appointments were made in accordance with the same. He urged that the learned Additional District Judge erred in law in setting aside and vacating the order of injunction granted by the trial Court without considering these facts on the documents filed by 'First' by the petitioner in consideration whereof the trial Court granted the order of injunction. Mr Farooqui urged that the documents filed before the trial Court being admitted documents the appellate Court below has erred in law by misreading mis-constructing and non-considering of those documents in setting aside the judgment and order of the trial Court. He submitted that non-consideration of the admitted documents being a question of law the appellate Court below has committed error of law in setting aside the trial Court judgment. He continued that the present suit being an open and shut one for decision of the suit depends upon the documents only consideration of the same in granting relief does not amount to giving decision on merit of the suit, but the appellate Court below has erred in law in finding that the trial Court has touched the merit of the suit in the interlocutory matter. He argued that the appellate Court below has erroneously found no prima facie and arguable case and the balance of convenience and inconvenience against the plaintiff and its finding that the plaintiff shall suffer no personal loss for the appointment of 546 employees, since they will to be provided by the University exchequer is misconceived. Inasmuch as, the appellate Court below failed to find that the instant suit is a public interest litigation (PIL) to safeguard the national interest in general and the interest of Rajshahi University in particular brought by a conscious citizen of the country for the reasons as aforesaid following the provision of Order I, rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure although there had been some omissions in complying the procedural provisions of the same which is technical and can be ignored for dispensation of justice. He urged strongly that the appellate Court below has set aside and vacated the trial Court order without reversing its findings and failing to find that the petitioner has brought the suit in public interest as a PIL and not for his personal interest, etc. 

 10. On the other hand, Mr AF Hassan Ariff, the learned Counsel appearing for the defendants-opposite parties 1-5, controverted the submissions of the learned Counsel of the petitioner, submitting that the suit itself is not maintainable in view of the provision of sections 42 and 56K of the Specific Relief Act and the plaintiff-petitioner is not entitled to get relief under Order XXXIX, rule 1 or under section 151 of the CPC. He submits that the civil Court is a creature of law and to be followed by the specific provisions embodied in the Code of Civil Procedure and the trial Court has illegally granted temporary injunction to the petitioner in a suit which is not maintainable and the plaintiff has no locus standi to file the suit. He argued that the suit being not maintainable and the petitioner being not entitled to get relief for aforesaid reasons, non-consideration of the documents filed by him for granting the relief does not arise in view of the fact that the petitioner has no personal right either to the property, office and to any contract with the Rajshahi University and there was no breach of such contract or evasion of right, or threat to office and, as such, the appellate Court below has not committed any error in setting aside the trial Court's order. He argues that the appellate Court below having committed no error this revisional application is not maintainable under the provision of section 115(1) of the CPC. Mr Ariff contends that no breach of contract having been made nor any personal right to property or office of the petitioner having been evaded by the University there does not arise any question of his suffering irreparable loss and balance of convenience and inconvenience in his favour and the question of a prima facie arguable case is far remote and the learned Additional District Judge having properly found the same against the petitioner rightly set aside and vacated the order of injunction. He also argued that section 151 of the CPC has no, manner of application in the instant case where particular procedural provision are available in the said Code. In support of his submission Mr Ariff has referred the cases of Chowmuhani College and another vs Md Ismail Hossain and others, reported in 26 DLR 10 and Prof MA Raquib & ors, vs Prof, Zillur Rahman & ors., reported in 37 DLR 83. 

 11. In reply Mr MI Farooqui, the learned Counsel for the petitioner, strongly rebutted the submissions made by Mr Hassan Ariff, saying that Mr Ariff admits error of law, misreading and misconstruction of the documents had the suit been filed according to the provisions of law mentioned by him which shows that there was a prima facie arguable case in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner causing violation and breach of rule, procedures, circulars, etc. as contained in the documents filed by petitioner and considered by the trial Court in granting temporary injunction. He submits that by non-considering the said documents the appellate Court has, therefore, committed error of law. He contends that section 42 nor section 56K is exhaustive and limited to the status or property to any person and, as such, the suit is maintainable. He also submits that in view of the provisions of section 9, Order I, rule 8 and Order XXXIX, rules I and 2 of the CPC the suit is maintainable having the plaintiff locus standi to file the suit in public interest. He canvassed that Code of Civil Procedure is an Act of 1908 made by the Britishers bringing the concept of PIL under Order I, rule 8 for the first time which is a procedural law and needs to be modified with the changing society but the same cannot over ride the substantive law. He argued that the technicality of procedure to be followed in bringing a proceeding in a Court of law should not stand as a bar in bringing such a suit. He strongly controverts that maintainability of the suit cannot be looked into except incidentally in interlocutory proceeding as a ground for rejecting temporary injunction. Mr Farooqui concludes strongly submitting that, since the petitioner in particular and the nation as a whole does not want to see Rajshahi University to face the unfortunate and saddest fate of Adamjee Jute Mills Ltd, the world's largest Jute Mill, a pride of Bangladesh and the unfortunate fate of ETV channel a most popular private electronic TV channel of the country shut down by the present Government due to crippled economy of the Mill and allegation of graft against ETV. He has brought this suit for justice and equity. 

 14. Plaintiff filed the suit in the public interest as a conscious citizen of the country to resist and protest the illegal and unfair appointments of 546 3rd and 4th Class employees in Rajshahi University on 15-4-2004. He filed the suit for declaration that such appointments are illegal and for permanent injunction restraining the defendant Nos. 1-5 form confirming such appointments, etc. He also filed an application under Order XXXIX, rule I read with section 151 of the CPC for res-training the defendant Nos. 1-5 from confirming the appointments, distributing duties and from giving them salaries. Defendants opposite party Nos. 1-5 contested the application by filing written objections, another set of written objection was filed by some other defendant-opposite parties mentioned above who, however, supported the plaintiff's case and did not contest the application for temporary injunction. Trial Court in consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, the written objections filed by the defendants and the documents filed by both the parties granted temporary injunction prima facie finding that the appointments have been made in breach and violation of the circulars, rules and procedures, guidelines, budgetary provision of the UGC, etc, and good arguable case, balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of the petitioner and that the University will sustain irreparable loss for such appointments. Trial Court also found that the new sets of 546 employees have also been posted to remove the existing incumbents most whimsically against the principle of natural justice and equity without any public advertisement, even without any post, demand and proposal from the concerned departments, etc. The learned Additional District Judge set aside and vacated the order of injunction in appeal. The appellate Court below found that it is not correct that appointments were made for personal interest and there was no necessity that any irregularities if made in the process of appointments the same would be decided in the suit on merit which cannot be considered at the time of passing an order of temporary injunction. The appellate Court below also found that there are official order of the authorities for such appointments and if such a good number of employees are barred from working the normal activities of the University could be hampered and, as such, the balance of convenience and inconvenience is against the petitioner and in favour of the defendants. The appellate Court below also found that there is no arguable prima facie case in favour of the plaintiff, since he will not suffer personal loss for the same and that the trial Court has touched the merit of the case in granting temporary injunction, etc. 

 15. Admittedly, the instant suit is a public interest litigation brought by the plaintiff in the interest of Rajshahi University. But on perusal of the appellate Court judgment, it appears that the appellate Court has thoroughly misconceived the suit and its spirit. The trial Court complying the guiding principles for passing an order of temporary injunction and being satisfied he granted the temporary injunction arriving at a clear prima facie finding in consideration of the documents filed that the appointments have been made in breach and violation of the circulars rules and procedures, guidelines, without public notification, etc. On the other hand, the appellate Court below has set aside and vacated the same putting much emphasis on the humanitarian ground rather than looking into the merit of rules and procedures, guidelines, budgetary provision, requirements, public notification, etc for making such huge appointments. It also appears that the finding of the appellate Court that the appointments were made in the necessity of the University is also without footing and not supported by any documents filed by the defendants. The appellate Court has totally failed to meet and revert the findings of the trial Court. The appellate Court below erroneously came to the finding on misreading and on misconstruction of the unlisted documents filed by the petitioner that, there is no prima facie arguable case and balance of convenience and inconvenience for the petitioner will not suffer any personal loss, misconceiving plaintiff's case. 

 16. Mr Ariff, the learned Counsel for the opposite party Nos. 1-5, instead of justifying the above findings of the appellate Court below on the facts of the case, assailed the finding of the trial Court and controverted the submissions of Mr Farooqui, the learned Counsel for the petitioner, has in his extensive submission basically confined himself on the maintainability of the suit itself and locus standi to file the suit by the plaintiff. 

 17. In support of his submissions, he referred two decisions already mentioned above. The substance of his submissions as aforesaid is that the plaintiff has no locus standi to file the suit and the same is not maintainable and hence, he is not entitled to set injunction. The decisions referred by him as mentioned above reported in 26 DLR 10 and in 37 DLR 83 are not applicable in the facts and circumstances and the points in issue for decision of the instant case. Both the above cases arose between the officer and the authorities of the institution out of its internal administrative order and decision and, as such, have no matter of application in the instant case. 

 18. This is a settled principle laid down by our Apex Court as well as the superior Courts of this sub-continent that the question of maintainability cannot be decided except looking into incidentally in an interlocutory matter which should be decreed on merit after taking evidence on trial. Mr Farooqui has referred a number of cases as mentioned above both in respect of findings on the maintainability of the suit in interlocutory mailer while granting and non-granting of an order of temporary injunction and to show that the suit is maintainable. On perusal of the decisions, I shall only say that those rulings are self-speaking on the points urged by Mr Farooqui but I refrained myself from quoting the aforesaid rulings and also from giving my findings and decision on the question of maintainability of the suit as to address his submission except that I am in quite agreement with the aforesaid rulings that the maintainability of the suit is a matter to be decided in the main suit on merit on trial and not in the interlocutory mailer. In agreement with the aforesaid ruling it is suffice to say that I find the suit prima facie maintainable and the petitioner is entitled to get the relief in law and no procedural technicality should stand in its way to get justice for the substance of the prayer has to be looked into rather than technicality. Incidentally, it may be mentioned that it has been held in the case between Abu Taher Chowdhury and others vs State, reported in 11 DLR (AD) 2 that "for promoting the cause of justice, for doing complete justice and for prevention of miscarriage of justice this Court's power is very wide, over riding and exceptional and is not encumbered by any technicality." In the case of Abdul Hamid Kazi vs Abdul Jabbar Jamadar and others, reported in 26 DLR (SC) 68. it has been held that "technicality of form, if adhered to, as the High Court took to be so, then there would be no proper dispensation of justice in the facts and circumstances of the case. In our view the substance of the prayer should be looked into taking an overall view of the facts and circumstances of the case, ignoring the mere technicality of form of the petition. So the views expressed by the learned Munsif in passing the order is in conformity with the substance of the petition filed by the appellant and it is not desired that the technicality of form should prevail causing impediment to dispensation of justice." 

 19. In view of the matter as above, I find no substance in the submission of Mr Ariff that since the suit is not maintainable and the plaintiff has no locus standi to file the same and that the documents filed by the plaintiff being not between him and the University, the appellate Court below has committed no error of law in not finding a prima facie arguable case and balance of convenience and inconvenience and question of irreparable loss of the plaintiff on considering those documents. I am quite unable to accept his submission inasmuch as misconstruction and misreading of document is a question of law. The appellate Court below has thus committed error of law in mis-constructing and misreading those documents. In the instant case, the documents being only reliable documents of facts and evidence for determining the issues involved in the suit non-construction and misreading of the same to find a prima facie arguable case and other principles required for granting temporary injunction, the same cannot be over looked by the Court. The whole submission of Mr Ariff as I have understood and already mentioned above that the plaintiff having no personal interest and right he is not entitled to an order of temporary injunction is, totally misconceived in the facts of the case where the plaintiff himself has disclosed in his plaint that he has filed the suit as a conscious citizen of the country in the interest of Rajshahi University in particular and in the interest of the nation in general. Therefore, where the plaintiff never claimed his personal interest any finding and submission centering round the same is misconceived and not maintainable. The appellate Court below has committed an error of law in failing to find a prima facie arguable case and balance of convenience and inconvenience and of suffering of irreparable loss by the University on the basis of the facts and documents. Humanitarian consideration and emotional thoughts cannot substitute legal consideration and ground for passing a judgment and order by the Court at the cost of the people of the country. The matter in issue has to be decided on merit of the suit on trial but till then the plaintiff-petitioner being able to make out a good prima facie arguable case is entitled to get temporary injunction so that no financial damage is caused to the University till disposal of the suit.
